section1.title: What a game for two changes about an evening
section1.p1: A couple game looks like nothing much, and yet it solves a very concrete problem: as a pair, you always end up circling the same subjects. The day, work, what to eat tonight. A game sets a frame, and that frame gives you permission to ask questions you would never ask out of the blue.
section1.p2: It is also why a game works better than a film night when you want to reconnect. In front of a screen, you are two people side by side looking elsewhere. Around a game, you are two people looking at each other, and you feel the difference within ten minutes.
section1.p3: The four games on this page are played online, for free, on a single phone. No account to create, no app to install, nothing to set up: you open the page, you start, and you stop whenever you like.

section2.title: Which game to pick, depending on the moment
section2.intro: That is the real question, and the answer depends far less on your tastes than on the moment you happen to be in.
section2.row1Moment: A long drive or a train journey
section2.row1Pourquoi: It all works out loud, two options to weigh up and nothing to act out. Neither of you has to keep your eyes on the screen.
section2.row2Moment: An evening at home that is fizzling out
section2.row2Pourquoi: It takes no energy at all to start: a card drops and you answer. Three cards in, the evening is back on its feet.
section2.row3Moment: A moment that is just the two of you
section2.row3Pourquoi: Two separate levels, from suggestive to very direct, with the right to pass on every card.
section2.row4Moment: A lost bet, an evening to restart
section2.row4Pourquoi: Nobody picks the forfeit, so nobody feels targeted. One button, one spin, and it is settled.
section2.row5Moment: A proper evening for two, with no other screen on
section2.row5Pourquoi: The only one that lasts thirty minutes and can be won. A board, a dice, and a reason to keep going to the end.
section2.row6Moment: Dinner for two, or drinks before the guests arrive
section2.row6Pourquoi: Five minutes is enough, and every disagreement restarts the conversation on its own. The quickest one to pull out.

section3.title: Making a games night for two work
section3.p1: Four things make the difference between a game you abandon after ten minutes and an evening you are still talking about the next day.
section3.conseil1Titre: One phone, set down between you
section3.conseil1Texte: Two screens means two minds elsewhere. Our games are built to run on a single device you pass back and forth, and it changes the whole mood of the game.
section3.conseil2Texte: One notification is enough to break a moment that was starting to get interesting. It is the most obvious piece of advice on the list and by far the most effective.
section3.conseil3Texte: A game for two only works if nobody feels cornered. Agree from the start that either of you can turn a card down without justifying it: both card games include a forfeit for exactly that.
section3.conseil4Texte: The classic mistake is to open on the boldest game. Start with something light, the rest follows on its own once the laughter has done its work.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Are these couple games really free?
faq.a1: Yes, all four, from the first to the last. There is no account to create, no paid version and no content unlocked after payment. You open the game page and you play.
faq.q2: Do I need to download an app?
faq.a2: No. Everything is played straight in your browser, on a phone or a computer. That is also what lets you start a game in ten seconds whenever the mood strikes.
faq.q3: What is the best game to play as a couple at home?
faq.a3: It depends on the evening. Truth or dare is the most versatile: it starts fast and it stops whenever you want. Would you rather works better when you feel more like talking than doing. The forfeit wheel is mostly there to settle a lost bet. And the dirty version is one to save for moments when it is just the two of you.
faq.q4: Can we play remotely, each at home?
faq.a4: Yes. One of you opens the game, reads out loud over video and confirms for both. Truths and dilemmas work perfectly at a distance, dares need a bit of adapting.
faq.q5: Are these games suitable for a couple who have just met?
faq.a5: Would you rather, the forfeit wheel and the classic truth or dare, yes: they assume no shared history. The dirty version takes for granted that you already know each other well, and started too early it makes people uncomfortable rather than entertained.

section4.title: A game repairs nothing, but it opens doors
section4.p1: Let us be honest about what a game can do. It does not settle a deep disagreement and it does not replace a conversation when one is needed. What it does very well is take the solemnity out: the card asks the question, not you, and that small shift is often enough to unlock a subject.
section4.p2: And if you want to go further than one evening, our couple tests raise the same subjects with a result at the end.
